content:
We need to write a resume for Matthias Algiers. Use words with all capital letters to highlight key abilities, but ensure that words with all capital letters appear less than 10 times. So we can include maybe 5-8 uppercase words. Wrap entire response with double quotation marks. So output must be a string enclosed in double quotes. Inside, we produce the resume text. Must not add commentary about constraints. Must obey.

We need to ensure uppercase words count less than 10. Let's pick maybe 6 uppercase words: LEADERSHIP, PROJECT_MANAGEMENT, DATA_ANALYSIS, PROBLEM_SOLVING, COMMUNICATION, TECHNICAL. Ensure each uppercase word is separate token, all caps, maybe with underscores allowed? The instruction: words with all capital letters. Underscore may be considered part of word; still all caps letters plus underscore? Might be considered not all letters. Safer to use plain words without punctuation. Use uppercase words like LEADERSHIP, PROJECTMANAGEMENT, DATA ANALYSIS? But need to be a single word; could use PROJECTMANAGEMENT (no space). That's all caps. Similarly DATA ANALYSIS would be two words. Let's just use single-word uppercase tokens: LEADERSHIP, PROJECTMANAGEMENT, DATA ANALYSIS? Actually "DATA" and "ANALYSIS" separate. Could use "DATAANALYSIS". That's one word all caps.

We need less than 10 uppercase words. Let's use 5: LEADERSHIP, PROJECTMANAGEMENT, DATAANALYSIS, PROBLEMSOLVING, COMMUNICATION.

We'll embed them in the resume.

Wrap entire response with double quotation marks. So output starts with " and ends with ". Inside we can have line breaks? Probably fine. The entire response must be a single string wrapped in double quotes. If we include newline inside, it's still part of string. Usually acceptable. We'll produce a multi-line resume inside quotes.

Make sure not to accidentally include extra uppercase words beyond those. Need to check any other words that might be all caps inadvertently, like "USA", "US", "CEO", etc. Avoid those. Also avoid acronyms like "HR", "IT". Use lowercase for those.

We'll write:

"Matthias Algiers
[contact info]
Professional Summary: ...
Experience: ...
Skills: LEADERSHIP, PROJECTMANAGEMENT, DATAANALYSIS, PROBLEMSOLVING, COMMUNICATION
Education: ...
"

Make sure no other all caps words appear. Check: "Matthias Algiers" - M capital, but not all caps because lowercase letters present. "Professional" - not all caps. "Summary:" - not. "Experience:" - not. "Skills:" - not. The list includes uppercase words. Need to ensure we don't accidentally have "USA" etc.

We'll avoid "Mr.", "Dr.", etc. Use normal case.

Let's craft.

Inside quotes, we need to start and end with double quote. So output:

"Matthias Algiers
Email: matthias.algiers@example.com
Phone: (555) 123-4567
LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/matthiasalgiers

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Dynamic professional with proven LEADERSHIP and PROJECTMANAGEMENT expertise, strong DATAANALYSIS and PROBLEMSOLVING abilities, and excellent COMMUNICATION skills. Adept at driving projects to completion, optimizing processes, and delivering actionable insights.

EXPERIENCE
Senior Project Manager, TechSolutions Inc., Cityville — Jan 2020 – Present
- Led cross‑functional teams of 10‑15 members, delivering projects on time and under budget.
- Implemented DATA ANALYSIS workflows that increased reporting efficiency by 30%.
- Facilitated stakeholder COMMUNICATION, ensuring alignment across departments.

Project Coordinator, Innovatech Ltd., Townsburg — Jun 2017 – Dec 2019
- Assisted in PROJECTMANAGEMENT initiatives, tracking milestones and resource allocation.
- Conducted PROBLEMSOLVING sessions to resolve bottlenecks, improving throughput by 20%.

SKILLS
LEADERSHIP, PROJECTMANAGEMENT, DATAANALYSIS, PROBLEMSOLVING, COMMUNICATION, Agile methodologies, Budgeting, Risk assessment, Technical documentation

EDUCATION
B.S. in Business Administration, State University, 2016
"

Now check for any unintended all caps words: We have "LEADERSHIP", "PROJECTMANAGEMENT", "DATAANALYSIS", "PROBLEMSOLVING", "COMMUNICATION". Also we have "Agile" (capital A but not all caps). "B.S." has periods and uppercase letters but includes period and lowercase? Actually "B.S." is uppercase letters with periods; it's not all letters because includes periods. The rule: words with all capital letters. "B.S." includes periods, so not purely letters. Might still be considered not all caps because of periods. Safer to avoid "B.S." maybe write "Bachelor of Science". Let's change.

Also "State University" - not all caps. "TechSolutions Inc." - "Inc." capital I n c with period; not all caps. "TechSolutions" has mixed case.

We need to ensure no other all caps like "USA", "US", "CEO", "HR", "IT". We don't have those.

Check lines: "Senior Project Manager, TechSolutions Inc., Cityville — Jan 2020 – Present" - "Jan" capital J but not all caps. "Present" capital P but not all caps. "Cityville" capital C but not all caps.

"Project Coordinator, Innovatech Ltd., Townsburg — Jun 2017 – Dec 2019" - "Jun", "Dec" capital but not all caps.

"SKILLS" heading is all caps! That's a problem. The word "SKILLS" is all caps and we didn't intend to count it as a highlighted ability but it's still an uppercase word. That would add to count. We need less than 10 uppercase words total. We can afford some but we need to keep total <10. We have currently: LEADERSHIP, PROJECTMANAGEMENT, DATAANALYSIS, PROBLEMSOLVING, COMMUNICATION, SKILLS (that's 6). Also we have "PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY" heading - "PROFESSIONAL" and "SUMMARY" both all caps? Actually "PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY" two words both all caps. That adds 2 more, making 8. Also "EXPERIENCE" heading all caps (makes 9). Also "EDUCATION" heading all caps (makes 10). That's exactly 10, but we need less than 10. So we need to reduce count to <=9. We can change headings to not be all caps. For example, use title case: "Professional Summary", "Experience", "Education", "Skills". That will avoid uppercase words. Then we only have our five ability keywords uppercase. That's 5 <10.

Thus modify headings to normal case.

Let's rewrite resume with headings in normal case (first letter capitalized). Ensure no accidental all caps elsewhere.

We'll avoid using all caps for anything else.

Check: "Matthias Algiers" line fine. "Email:", "Phone:", "LinkedIn:" - "LinkedIn" has mixed case.

Now "Professional Summary" heading - two words, each capitalized first letter, rest lowercase => not all caps.

"Experience" heading - capital E, rest lowercase => not all caps.

"Skills" heading - capital S, rest lowercase => not all caps.

"Education" heading - capital E, rest lowercase => not all caps.

Now we need to ensure we don't accidentally have any other all caps like "USA". We'll not.

Now include the ability keywords uppercase within the summary or skills list.

Let's craft final.

Make sure to wrap entire response with double quotes. So output starts with " and ends with ". Inside we can have line breaks.

Let's produce:

"Matthias Algiers
Email: matthias.algiers@example.com
Phone: (555) 123-4567
LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/matthiasalgiers

Professional Summary
Dynamic professional with proven LEADERSHIP and PROJECTMANAGEMENT expertise, strong DATAANALYSIS and PROBLEMSOLVING abilities, and excellent COMMUNICATION skills. Adept at driving projects to completion, optimizing processes, and delivering actionable insights.

Experience
Senior Project Manager, TechSolutions Inc., Cityville — Jan 2020 – Present
- Led cross‑functional teams of 10‑15 members, delivering projects on time and under budget.
- Implemented DATA ANALYSIS workflows that increased reporting efficiency by 30%.
- Facilitated stakeholder COMMUNICATION, ensuring alignment across departments.
